A1.justification: These are identifiable versions of the same pathology-embedding work despite extensive revision and renaming. All supplied pages, equations, tables and figures support comparison. Neither PDF contains appendices; both reference separate supplementary material that is unavailable here.

before.justification: v2 Tables 2–5 and Figures 4–5 report original retrieval, classification, embedding-alignment and ablation results.

after.justification: v3 Tables 2–6 and Figures 3–4 report original composed retrieval, simple retrieval, classification, qualitative and component-ablation results.

M1.justification: HOMIE substantially revises MLLM4PUE: LLaVA-NeXT-8B with fixed-resolution inputs becomes Qwen2.5-VL-7B with native-resolution processing. v3 adds text-only retrieval adaptation, subsequent pathology tuning, a morphology-to-diagnosis curriculum, bootstrap filtering and stain normalization/augmentation. These change the procedure beyond renaming or expanded explanation.

E1.justification: v3 adds multi-image-to-text, image-text-to-image and video-to-text evaluation, plus Educontent and MMUpubmed simple retrieval. DigestPath's two classification tasks and Wsss4luad disappear. Training adds MedNLI/MedMCQA text pairs and PathGen-1.6M. Bookset/Pubmedset retain the cited sources of Arch-book/Arch-PubMed; those name changes alone are not new coverage.

E2.justification: Beyond the retained E5-V, PLIP, PathCLIP and QuiltNet, v3 evaluates PubmedCLIP, BiomedCLIP, Pathgen-CLIP variants, Patho-CLIP variants, MUSK, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, LamRA and GME. CONCH expands from classification-only comparison in v2 to retrieval comparisons. Conversely, QuiltNet is no longer included in the fusion ablation.

E3.justification: Evaluation sizes change substantially: LCcolon increases from 1,000 to 10,000 samples, and Bookset from 1,306 to 2,688. Retrieval reporting changes from R@5/10/50 to R@1/5/10; classification changes from wF1 and accuracy to an undefined 'weighted accuracy.' Training budgets and input processing change, GPT-5 replaces the earlier ChatGPT cleaning description, and explicit training-data-matched comparisons are no longer provided.

E4.justification: v3 adds filtering, curriculum, stain-processing and resolution ablations, plus qualitative retrieval cases. Fusion analysis covers additional query types but removes question-only controls. The modality-gap study changes from t-SNE on Arch datasets against PathCLIP to UMAP on Educontent against several baselines. v2's sample-size robustness analysis is absent from the supplied v3.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. v3's bootstrap procedure filters training data; it does not introduce statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Results are extensively replaced and expanded. v2 Table 4 reports MLLM4PUE-Q R@5 of 47.5%/67.5% on Quilt-VQA/RED; v3 Table 2 reports HOMIE at 67.1%/87.7%. These involve changed models, training and answer processing, not controlled same-setting gains. Newly reported results include 78.5% multi-image-to-text and 30.7% video-to-text R@1.

T1.justification: v2 Equation 1 explicitly sums image-to-text and text-to-image contrastive terms. v3 Section 3.4 instead displays a batch-averaged query-to-candidate objective without a reverse term. Section 3.1 also formalizes the broader PCR input/candidate definition, including videos and interleaved inputs. Neither version provides theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from broadly reusable pathology embeddings and PMEB to defining expanded Pathology Composed Retrieval and adapting MLLMs through a two-stage HOMIE framework. The abstract, introduction and conclusion now emphasize interleaved modalities, task/domain mismatch and retrieval as a clinical computational consult.

C2.justification: v2 emphasizes data efficiency, modality alignment and the adequacy of sampled evaluation. v3 introduces stronger explanations based on morphology-first learning and claims that every adaptation component is essential. It attributes CONCH's Pubmedset advantage to likely training/test overlap without reporting an overlap audit, and identifies genomics integration as future work.

D1.justification: v3 documents stage-specific corpus sizes, trained modules, batch sizes of 576/384, learning rates of 4e-5/1e-4, two-epoch schedules and eight H100 GPUs instead of six. Earlier QLoRA, checkpointing, DeepSpeed and temperature disclosures are no longer stated. The new filtering threshold remains unspecified, and referenced benchmark-construction prompts are unavailable.

R1.justification: Related work expands substantially to MUSK, Pathgen/Patho-CLIP, VLM2Vec, LamRA and GME, positioning HOMIE against both pathology encoders and general multimodal retrievers. The introduction replaces much of the broad diagnostic-task motivation with literature on retrieval, interpretability, hallucination and clinician decision support.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method narrative and conclusion are extensively rewritten around HOMIE/PCR. Results move into the experiments section, composed retrieval becomes the leading evaluation, and the separate zero-shot-transfer explanation is replaced by architecture, adaptation and training-objective sections. This exceeds terminology or numbering changes.

P2.justification: v3 adds a clinical-retrieval workflow to Figure 1, redraws the architecture overview, introduces qualitative examples and replaces the modality-gap plots. Results tables are reordered and substantially restructured; the sample-size chart disappears and component-ablation displays are added. Figure 4 also introduces a caption/legend disagreement over image/text colors.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens empirical support for composed retrieval through distinct multi-image/video tests, more competitive baselines and component controls (Tables 2–6), addressing v2's narrow composed-query validation. The gain is tempered by losing training-data-matched comparisons, incomplete reproducibility details and overstated interpretations: the stain ablation changes composed R@1 only from 53.2 to 53.1, and CONCH overlap is unverified. Nevertheless, the stronger testing of capabilities and design choices constitutes a substantial overall improvement.
